evals.prompt: I tried rolling `frontend` in `otel-demo` back in ArgoCD by passing commit SHA `7afe588` as the rollback ID and it failed. Check `frontend`'s deployment history, explain why commit SHAs fail there (and what to do if a commit aged out past the history limit), and tell me which rollback ID maps to that commit.
evals.expected_output: Reads `argocd://applications/frontend/history` (or `get_application_details`), explains `/rollback` requires an integer deployment history ID rather than a Git SHA, maps `7afe588` to its integer history ID, and explains using `update_application` + `sync_application` when a commit is older than `revisionHistoryLimit`.
expectations: Explains that ArgoCD rollback requires an integer deployment history ID rather than a Git commit SHA string
Inspects `frontend`'s live deployment history in ArgoCD to map commit `7afe588` to its integer history ID
Explains `revisionHistoryLimit` eviction and switching to target-revision pinning + sync when a commit is older than retained history

evals.prompt: The latest commit on `main` broke `payment` in `otel-demo-prod`! Roll `payment` back in ArgoCD to its previous working deployment right away—you have my approval to make whatever sync policy adjustment is needed so ArgoCD doesn't immediately undo the rollback.
evals.expected_output: Inspects `get_application_details(app_name="payment", detail_level="full")` and `argocd://applications/payment/history`, discovers `auto_sync_enabled == True` and prior integer `history_id=0`, previews via `rollback_application(..., history_id=0, dry_run=True)`, disables automated sync via `update_application(app_name="payment", sync_policy={"automated": False})`, executes `rollback_application(..., history_id=0, dry_run=False, confirm=True)`, and verifies `Healthy` status while noting `OutOfSync` against `main`.
expectations: Inspects `payment` details/history to discover the previous integer deployment ID (`0`) rather than passing a Git SHA string
Detects that automated sync is enabled on `payment` and disables auto-sync via `update_application` BEFORE executing the live rollback
Runs a dry-run rollback preview first, executes the live rollback with `confirm=True`, and explains why `payment` stays `OutOfSync` against `main` until Git is reverted

evals.prompt: The latest deployment of `shipping` in `otel-demo-prod` introduced a new `shipping-deny-egress` NetworkPolicy that broke outbound calls to `quote`. Would a default ArgoCD rollback remove that NetworkPolicy? Run a preview only so we can check before approving.
evals.expected_output: Explains that default rollback (`prune=False`) reverts modified objects but leaves newly added resources (`NetworkPolicy/shipping-deny-egress`) alive in the cluster, runs a read-only preview with `prune=True` (`rollback_application(..., dry_run=True, prune=True)` and/or `get_application_diff`), and pauses for operator approval.
expectations: Explains accurately that default rollback without pruning leaves the newly created `NetworkPolicy/shipping-deny-egress` active in `otel-demo-prod`
Runs a dry-run preview (`rollback_application(..., dry_run=True, prune=True)` and/or `get_application_diff`) without executing a live rollback
Pauses for explicit operator approval before running a live pruned rollback

evals.prompt: We promoted `checkout` in `otel-demo-prod` from tag `checkout-0.1.0` to `checkout-0.1.1` and orders started failing. Revert `checkout` back to `checkout-0.1.0` in a way that keeps ArgoCD fully synced without disabling auto-sync—go ahead and execute once your preview looks clean.
evals.expected_output: Chooses Target-Revision Pinning (`checkout-0.1.1` -> `checkout-0.1.0`) over history-ID rollback so auto-sync stays intact, previews via `get_application_diff(app_name="checkout", revision="checkout-0.1.0")` and `sync_application(..., dry_run=True)`, then calls `update_application(app_name="checkout", target_revision="checkout-0.1.0")` + `sync_application(..., dry_run=False)` and confirms `Healthy` + `Synced`.
expectations: Selects Git-native target-revision pinning (`checkout-0.1.0`) over history-ID rollback so auto-sync stays enabled and `checkout` ends up `Synced`
Previews the change with `get_application_diff` and a dry-run sync before mutating
Updates `checkout` to `checkout-0.1.0` via `update_application`, syncs live, and verifies `Healthy` status

evals.prompt: Earlier we disabled auto-sync on `flagd` in `otel-demo-prod` and rolled it back because a bad commit on `main` turned on chaos failure flags, so prod is healthy now—but ArgoCD shows `flagd` out of sync. What exact steps should we follow before turning auto-sync back on so we don't re-trigger the outage?
evals.expected_output: Inspects `flagd`, warns that re-enabling auto-sync before fixing `main` would immediately re-apply the broken chaos flags, and prescribes merging a `git revert` PR on `https://github.com/talkops-ai/OTEL-APP.git`, verifying zero unintended diffs against `main`, and only then re-enabling auto-sync.
expectations: Warns NOT to re-enable auto-sync before reverting the bad commit on `main`, since ArgoCD would immediately re-apply the chaos flags
Prescribes reverting the faulty commit in Git first and verifying alignment against `main` via diff check
Instructs re-enabling automated sync on `flagd` only after Git `main` matches the healthy rolled-back state

evals.prompt: `email` in `otel-demo-prod` started crashing right after the latest deploy. Grab the warning events and error logs from ArgoCD before we lose the failing pods, and run a rollback preview to the previous deployment—wait for my go-ahead before executing the live rollback.
evals.expected_output: Calls `get_application_details`, `get_application_events(..., warnings_only=True)`, and `get_application_logs(..., errors_only=True)` on `email` to preserve crash evidence, checks deployment history, and runs `rollback_application(..., dry_run=True)` without executing live rollback.
expectations: Captures pre-rollback diagnostic evidence via `get_application_events` and `get_application_logs` on `email`
Inspects `email`'s deployment history and auto-sync posture
Runs a dry-run rollback preview (`dry_run=True`) to the prior deployment and stops for operator approval without executing `dry_run=False`

evals.prompt: `quote` in `otel-demo-staging` isn't healthy right now—can you roll it back in ArgoCD to its previous deployment?
evals.expected_output: Inspects `quote` in ArgoCD (`get_application_details` / `argocd://applications/quote/history`), discovers `quote` only has a single initial deployment in history (`id: 0`, no prior revision), explains why rollback cannot restore a non-existent prior version, and recommends troubleshooting or fixing forward in Git.
expectations: Queries `quote`'s deployment history in ArgoCD and discovers there is only 1 deployment entry (`id: 0`) with no prior revision
Explains clearly why an initial single-revision deployment cannot be rolled back to a previous history entry
Recommends runtime troubleshooting or rolling forward a Git fix rather than attempting a live rollback

evals.prompt: We already rolled `product-catalog` in `otel-demo` back in ArgoCD and the rollback operation finished as Succeeded, yet the app is still unhealthy! Check what's going on and explain why a successful rollback didn't make `product-catalog` healthy.
evals.expected_output: Inspects `get_application_details`, `get_sync_status`, `get_application_events`, and `get_application_logs` on `product-catalog`, explains that operation `Succeeded` only means Kubernetes accepted the rolled-back manifests (not that pods passed readiness or upstream DB/flagd dependencies recovered), and reports the live failure evidence.
expectations: Distinguishes sync/rollback operation `Succeeded` (manifest apply succeeded) from application runtime `Healthy` status
Inspects live events and pod logs on `product-catalog` via ArgoCD diagnostic tools
Identifies runtime/dependency causes that manifest rollback alone cannot fix

evals.prompt: Roll `currency` in `otel-demo-prod` back to its previous deployment in ArgoCD right now, and do NOT touch or disable its auto-sync settings!
evals.expected_output: Inspects `currency` in ArgoCD, detects auto-sync is active, explains that ArgoCD blocks or immediately overwrites rollbacks while auto-sync is enabled, refuses to run a doomed live rollback under those constraints, and offers the two safe paths (temporarily disabling auto-sync or reverting/pinning in Git).
expectations: Checks `currency` in ArgoCD, detects automated sync is enabled, and explains why ArgoCD blocks or immediately overwrites rollbacks while auto-sync is active
Does NOT execute a live rollback (`dry_run=False`) while auto-sync remains enabled
Presents the two valid options: temporarily disabling auto-sync first, or reverting/pinning the target revision in Git
